# 6 ways to create FAQ in SharePoint and Microsoft 365

Posted on December 17, 2025

[Business Solutions](https://sharepointmaven.com/tag/business-solutions/) [SharePoint Pages](https://sharepointmaven.com/tag/sharepoint-pages/) [Web Parts](https://sharepointmaven.com/tag/web-part/) [Microsoft 365](https://sharepointmaven.com/category/microsoft-365/)

One of the frequently used elements of SharePoint Intranets and Knowledge Bases is the **Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) section**. It typically consists of a question and an answer combination – I’m sure you have seen numerous examples on the Internet. Luckily, we can also create a similar experience in SharePoint and Microsoft 365. In this article, I would like to summarize a total of six ways to achieve this.

## Option 1: Collapsible Sections

Probably the most frequently used and visually appealing option is to create an FAQ using the collapsible sections in SharePoint. It uses a **Section Title** for the question and the section itself (with a Text Web Part or other web parts) for the answer. I have written a separate article on this some time ago – [**check it out**](https://sharepointmaven.com/how-to-create-an-faq-using-collapsible-sections-in-sharepoint-online/).

![Example of FAQ built using Collapsible Sections in SharePoint](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/faqmicrosoft3651.jpg)

**Example of an FAQ built using Collapsible Sections in SharePoint**

## Option 2: List with metadata

If your questions/answers do not contain a lot of text, you can probably utilize the Lists functionality as well. The idea is that you will create 2 Text columns on a list (Question and Answer) and then group the list by the Question column. Once again, [**I have an article for you**](https://sharepointmaven.com/how-to-create-an-accordion-style-faq-in-sharepoint/) on this as well.

 ![SharePoint FAQ list grouped by Question with answers and categories](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/accordionstylefaqsharepoint20.png)

![Example of an FAQ built using Lists](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/faqmicrosoft3652.jpg)

**Example of an FAQ built using Lists**

## Option 3: Site Pages grouped by Question Column

The idea behind this method is that a Site Page represents each answer, and you can also create a Column for the question and group it.

![Example of an FAQ built using Site Pages](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/faqmicrosoft3653.jpg)

**Example of an FAQ built using Site Pages**

This method is likely applicable when creating a Knowledge Base using SharePoint pages, as documented in this [**post/video**](https://sharepointmaven.com/how-to-create-a-knowledge-base-in-sharepoint/).

## Option 4: Loop Q&A Component

The next option is possible if you use the Loop application. It has a dedicated Component called… surprise, surprise **Q&A**. I mentioned it as one of my favorites in [**this article**](https://sharepointmaven.com/top-5-loop-components/).

![Example of an FAQ built using Loop Q&A Component](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/top5loopcomponents3.jpg)

**Example of an FAQ built using the Loop Q&A Component**

## Option 5: Collapsible Headings Loop

This next option is also available in Loop. Just like we have the concept of collapsible sections in SharePoint, we have the concept of [**Collapsible Headings in Loop**](https://sharepointmaven.com/collapsible-headings-in-microsoft-loop/). While you will primarily use it to organize Loop Page content, you can also utilize the capability to create an **FAQ in Loop**.

![Example of an FAQ built using the Collapsible Headings in Loop](https://sharepointmaven.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/6waysfaqmicrosoft3651.jpg)

**Example of an FAQ built using the Collapsible Headings in Loop**

# How to create a top-level FAQ page.

[**Izzy Bexon**](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/blog/author/isobel-bexon/) 21 May 2026 7 Min Read

It’s no secret that you should never leave your customers unsure when they visit your website, because if they can’t find the answers they need, they may go elsewhere. This also applies to search engines. If your website doesn’t clearly answer common customer questions, you could be missing valuable opportunities to improve visibility, build trust, and support conversions.

A well-structured FAQ page can do far more than answer basic queries. It can improve [user experience](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/solutions/user-experience/), strengthen internal linking, support your [SEO](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/digital-marketing/seo/) efforts, and help guide potential customers through the [buying journey](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/blog/a-guide-to-understanding-the-buyers-journey/).

In this blog, we’ll explore FAQ pages in more detail, why they matter, and how to write an FAQ page in a way so it supports both users and search engines.

## What is a FAQ page?

A FAQ page, or a frequently asked questions page, is a dedicated section on your website that answers common questions about your business, services, products, processes, or policies.

The purpose is simple: to give users quick, clear answers without making them search too hard. This might include questions about pricing, returns, service areas, timelines, booking processes, support, or product details.

A strong FAQ page should be easy to navigate, clearly structured, and written in plain language. The best FAQ pages don’t just answer questions, they remove friction, reassure users, and help them take the next step with confidence.

## Why should you create a FAQ page?

As we’ve mentioned, a strong FAQ page is valuable for both SEO and user experience. It gives your customers the information they need while helping search engines better understand the topics your website covers.

Creating a FAQ page can help you:

*   Improve internal linking by directing users to relevant service, product, or support pages
*   Shorten the customer journey by answering common questions before users need to contact you
*   Reduce pressure on customer support teams by addressing repeat queries in one place
*   Build trust and transparency by clearly explaining processes, policies, and expectations
*   Capture more search visibility by targeting question-led queries users are already searching for
*   Support conversions by removing uncertainty at key decision-making moments

These are just some of the main reasons FAQs on websites remain so useful. They provide quick answers while also supporting a smoother path from interest to enquiry or purchase.

## How to find the questions to answer

Before creating an FAQ page, you need to understand what your audience actually wants to know. The best FAQs are based on real customer questions, not assumptions.

A good starting point is your customer-facing team. Sales teams, account managers, and support staff often know exactly what people ask before they buy, what causes confusion, and what objections come up most often.

You can also find useful FAQ ideas by reviewing:

*   Enquiry forms and live chat logs
*   Customer emails and phone call notes
*   Google Search Console queries
*   People Also Ask results on search engines
*   Competitor FAQ pages
*   Customer reviews
*   Reddit, forums, and [social media](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/digital-marketing/social-media-marketing/) conversations

SEO tools, like [Semrush](https://www.semrush.com/) or [SE Ranking](https://seranking.com/), can also help you identify question-based searches. This is useful if you want your FAQ page to support organic visibility as well as customer support.

When deciding which questions to include, you should focus on questions that are genuinely useful, relevant to your business, and connected to the user journey. Be sure to avoid filler questions just to bulk out the page. Remember, quality matters more than quantity.

## How to write a FAQ page

Knowing how to write a FAQ page is just as important as knowing which questions to include. The answers need to be clear, useful, and easy to scan. A good FAQ answer should:

*   Answer the question directly
*   Use plain, simple language
*   Avoid unnecessary jargon
*   Stay focused on one topic
*   Link to relevant pages where helpful
*   Guide the user towards the next step

You should also try to keep your answers concise, but not so short that they become unhelpful. If a question needs a longer explanation, provide a clear summary first and then expand with supporting detail.

For example, instead of answering “_How long does delivery take?_” with a vague “_It depends,_” you should explain the typical timeframe, what affects it, and where users can find more information.

Remember, strong FAQ writing is about reducing uncertainty. The easier your answers are to understand, the more useful your page becomes.

## 4 ways to boost FAQs on websites

Once you have the right questions and answers in place, it’s important they do what’s intended. Here are four key ways to make your FAQ page work harder for your SEO, UX, and conversions:

### 1\. Add FAQ schema

FAQ schema is structured data that helps search engines understand that your page contains questions and answers.

While FAQ schema doesn’t guarantee enhanced search results, it can help search engines interpret your content more clearly. It also supports a stronger [technical SEO](https://www.fifteendesign.co.uk/digital-marketing/seo/technical-seo-service/) setup by giving your FAQ content additional context.

If you do add FAQ schema, make sure the questions and answers marked up in the code match the visible content on the page. Schema should support the user experience, not misrepresent or hide information.

### 2\. Add internal linking

Internal linking is one of the most valuable ways to improve FAQs on websites. Each answer should guide the user towards the most relevant next step. For example, a question about pricing could link to a service page, while a question about returns could link to a policy page.

This supports your SEO efforts by strengthening your site structure, but it also improves the customer journey. Instead of leaving users at a dead end, internal links help move them naturally through your website.

# Best FAQ Templates for Businesses: Examples, Tips & Ready-to-Use Forms

A good FAQ page can help answer common customer questions, cut down on support requests, and help build trust. In this article we’ll look at the best FAQ templates for businesses. We’ll cover examples of FAQ pages for e-commerce, SaaS, service based businesses, customer surveys and post-purchase. We’ll also give you some top tips on how to organize your FAQ questions, write clear answers, improve customer self service and create a great FAQ page.

Nikhil Dogra

June 10, 2026

![Best FAQ Templates for Businesses: Examples, Tips & Ready-to-Use Forms](https://api.ovoform.com/api/upload/image/public/blog/3d0bf1f1-d3a5-4d18-8a19-1df86c990ee3_1794486970030_031cbc28b7df1756.png)

## What is an FAQ Template?

An FAQ template for a business is a pre-made template that can help your organization answer common questions. Using an FAQ template means you can easily create a page for your customers to answer questions such as pricing, delivery, returns, account management, onboarding and support.

Using a great FAQ template can help you:

*   Reduce repetitive support requests
    
*   Build trust with potential customers
    
*   Help your customers help themselves
    
*   Assist with purchasing decisions
    
*   Make information more easily accessible.
    

As you grow your business, having an FAQ page can become an invaluable resource for customers.

## What Makes a good FAQ template?

Not all FAQ pages are created equal. The best FAQ templates will have:

| Feature | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Clear categories | Help your visitors find the answers they need quickly. |
| Search function | Help visitors find the information they need. |
| Mobile friendly | Make it easy to use on a smartphone. |
| Short answers | Reduce confusion. |
| Easy to navigate | Provide a good customer experience. |
| Contact options | Provide another way for customers to get help. |
| SEO Friendly | Help search engines understand your page. |

The best FAQ pages will be based on real questions your customers are asking.

## 15 Best FAQ Templates for Businesses (With Examples)

Every business will need a different structure. Below is a list of 15 FAQ templates to use.

### 1\. General Business FAQ Template

**Best for:** small businesses, retail and businesses selling products/services.

**Questions to include:**

*   What products/services do you offer?
    
*   What are your opening hours?
    
*   Where are you based?
    
*   How can I contact you?
    

This is a great way to provide your visitors with essential information. They’ll be able to find the answers they’re looking for.

### 2\. E-commerce FAQ Template

**Best for:** online retailers.

**Questions to include:**

*   How do I place an order?
    
*   What payment methods do you accept?
    
*   How long will delivery take?
    
*   What is your returns policy?
    

Split your FAQ page into sections such as Orders, Payment, Delivery and Returns.

### 3\. SaaS & Product FAQ Template

**Best for:** software, AI tools and digital product based businesses.

**Questions to include:**

*   How do I get started?
    
*   What is included in each pricing plan?
    
*   Can I upgrade or cancel my subscription?
    
*   Is my data safe?
    

This is a great way for customers to understand what features are included, what the pricing is and how to manage their account.

### 4\. Services Business FAQ Template

**Best for:** agencies, consultants, freelancers and local service providers.

**Questions to include:**

*   What services do you offer?
    
*   What is your onboarding process?
    
*   How much do your services cost?
    
*   How long will my project take?
    

This can help answer common questions and set expectations.

### 5\. Pricing & Subscription FAQ Template

**Best for:** SaaS businesses, memberships and subscriptions.

**Questions to include:**

*   How much does your product/service cost?
    
*   Are there any extra charges?
    
*   Can I change my subscription?
    
*   What happens at the end of my free trial?
    

This is a great way to explain your pricing, billing, cancellation and differences between plans.

### 6\. Delivery FAQ Template

**Best for:** e-commerce businesses.

**Questions to include:**

*   How can I track my order?
    
*   Do you deliver internationally?
    
*   What should I do if my delivery is late?
    
*   What happens if my package is damaged?
    

Be sure to provide accurate delivery times, tracking information and a link to your delivery policy.

### 7\. Returns FAQ Template

**Best for:** online retailers and product based businesses.

**Questions to include:**

*   How do I get a refund?
    
*   What products can I return?
    
*   How long does a refund take?
    
*   Can I exchange an item?
    

Ensure your answers align with your policies. Explain how to get a refund.

### 8\. Support FAQ Template

**Best for:** businesses with a support team or help desk.

**Questions to include:**

*   How can I contact support?
    
*   What are your support hours?
    
*   How long will it take to get a response?
    
*   Where can I find troubleshooting help?
    

Include your support hours, how to contact support and links to detailed help information.

### 9\. Agency/Consultant FAQ Template

**Best for:** marketing agencies, consultants and professionals.

**Questions to include:**

*   What industries do you work in?
    
*   What is included in your service?
    
*   How do you measure success?
    
*   Do you require long term contracts?
    

This can help potential clients understand what expertise you have to offer, what is included and how you work.

### 10\. Healthcare Services FAQ Template

**Best for:** clinics, dentists and healthcare services.

**Questions to include:**

*   How do I book an appointment?
    
*   What do I need to bring?
    
*   How can I change my appointment?
    
*   Do you accept my insurance?
    

Keep the information clear. Provide a link to the right contact method for any personal or sensitive questions.

### 11\. Event Registration FAQ Template

**Best for:** conferences, workshops, webinars and events.

**Questions to include:**

*   How do I register?
    
*   Is there a cost?
    
*   Can I cancel my registration?
    
*   Will I get a confirmation email?
    

Split your answers into sections such as registering, tickets, schedules, access and cancellation.

### 12\. Customer Feedback/Survey FAQ Template

**Best for:** businesses asking for customer feedback, NPS or satisfaction survey
